question:
A 39-year-old Indian woman seeks fertility consultation with her spouse due to difficulty conceiving.
She met her current husband during humanitarian work in Nepal a decade ago. Her symptoms include
chronic vague lower abdominal discomfort and menstrual irregularities, including spotting and passage
of blood clots over recent months. She reports no dyspareunia, post-coital bleeding, malodorous
vaginal discharge, fever, or weight loss. Physical examination reveals mild cervical bleeding and slight
tenderness on bimanual examination without palpable masses. A hysterosalpingogram reveals sinus
tract formation and peritubal adhesions. A menstrual fluid sample is sent for microbiological analysis.
Which pathogen is the most probable cause of her presentation? Answer Choices: (A) *Mycoplasma
genitalium* (B) *Klebsiella granulomatis* (C) *Treponema pallidum* (D) *Chlamydia trachomatis* (E)
*Escherichia coli* (F) *Ureaplasma urealyticum* (G) *Actinomyces israelii* (H) *Trichomonas vaginalis*
(I) *Mycobacterium tuberculosis* (J) *Neisseria gonorrhoeae*
 A. *Ureaplasma urealyticum*
B. *Treponema pallidum*
C. *Chlamydia trachomatis*
D. *Mycobacterium tuberculosis*
E. *Actinomyces israelii*
F. *Neisseria gonorrhoeae*

G. *Escherichia coli*
H. *Klebsiella granulomatis*
I. *Mycoplasma genitalium*
J. *Trichomonas vaginalis*
